| Venule | 40 |
| Vein | 15 |

explanation.text: By conservation of volumetric flow rate ($Q = A_{\text{aorta}} v_{\text{aorta}} = A_{\text{cap}} v_{\text{cap}}$), the velocity of blood in the capillaries is $v_{\text{cap}} = v_{\text{aorta}} \frac{A_{\text{aorta}}}{A_{\text{cap}}} = 30\text{ cm/s} \times \frac{4.5\text{ cm}^2}{4500\text{ cm}^2} = 0.03\text{ cm/s} = 0.3\text{ mm/s}$. The transit time through a capillary of length $L = 0.5\text{ mm}$ is $t = \frac{L}{v_{\text{cap}}} = \frac{0.5\text{ mm}}{0.3\text{ mm/s}} = \frac{5}{3}\text{ s} \approx 1.67\text{ s}$.

questions.original_text: A DNA extract solution with a concentration of 15 ng/uL placed in a micro-cuvette of sample thickness 0.5 mm gave an absorbance of 0.24 at a wavelength of 260 nm in a spectrophotometer. After further concentration, the sample was found to give an absorbance of 0.38 at the same wavelength under identical conditions. The final concentration of the sample is ________ ng/uL. (Give your answer rounded off to 2 decimal places.)
questions.display_text: A DNA extract solution with a concentration of $15\text{ ng/}\mu\text{L}$ placed in a micro-cuvette of sample thickness $0.5\text{ mm}$ gave an absorbance of $0.24$ at a wavelength of $260\text{ nm}$ in a spectrophotometer. After further concentration, the sample was found to give an absorbance of $0.38$ at the same wavelength under identical conditions. The final concentration of the sample is ________ $\text{ng/}\mu\text{L}$. (Give your answer rounded off to 2 decimal places.)

explanation.text: By the Beer-Lambert Law, absorbance $A = \varepsilon c l$ is directly proportional to concentration $c$ when path length $l$ and wavelength are fixed: $\frac{c_2}{c_1} = \frac{A_2}{A_1}$. Thus, $c_2 = 15 \times \frac{0.38}{0.24} = 23.75\text{ ng/}\mu\text{L}$.

questions.original_text: An X-ray beam of initial intensity I0 of 70 keV imaging the chest is assumed to undergo attenuation through the muscle tissue for a thickness of 16 cm and further through the bone tissue for a thickness of 4 cm. The half value layer (HVL) thicknesses for the muscle and bone are 3.5 cm and 1.8 cm, respectively. The percentage of X-ray intensity transmitted through the body is ________. Give your answer rounded off to 2 decimal places.
questions.display_text: An X-ray beam of initial intensity $I_0$ of $70\text{ keV}$ imaging the chest is assumed to undergo attenuation through the muscle tissue for a thickness of $16\text{ cm}$ and further through the bone tissue for a thickness of $4\text{ cm}$. The half value layer (HVL) thicknesses for the muscle and bone are $3.5\text{ cm}$ and $1.8\text{ cm}$, respectively. The percentage of X-ray intensity transmitted through the body is ________. Give your answer rounded off to 2 decimal places.

explanation.text: The number of half-value layers traversed is $n_{\text{muscle}} = \frac{16}{3.5} \approx 4.5714$ and $n_{\text{bone}} = \frac{4}{1.8} \approx 2.2222$, for a total of $n_{\text{total}} = \frac{16}{3.5} + \frac{4}{1.8} = \frac{428}{63} \approx 6.79365$ HVLs. The percentage of transmitted intensity is $\frac{I}{I_0} \times 100\% = \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{6.79365} \times 100\% \approx 0.9001\% \approx 0.90\%$.

questions.original_text: A person standing one meter away from a 4000 curie radioactive source receives a lethal dose of radiation in about 5 minutes. At 3 meters away from the same source, the time in which he will receive the same lethal dose is ________ minutes. Give your answer rounded off to the nearest integer.
questions.display_text: A person standing one meter away from a $4000\text{ curie}$ radioactive source receives a lethal dose of radiation in about $5\text{ minutes}$. At $3\text{ meters}$ away from the same source, the time in which he will receive the same lethal dose is ________ minutes. Give your answer rounded off to the nearest integer.

explanation.text: By the inverse-square law for radiation intensity (dose rate $\dot{D} \propto \frac{1}{r^2}$), the accumulated dose is $D = \dot{D} t \propto \frac{t}{r^2}$. For the same total lethal dose at $r_2 = 3\text{ m}$ vs. $r_1 = 1\text{ m}$: $t_2 = t_1 \left(\frac{r_2}{r_1}\right)^2 = 5 \times \left(\frac{3}{1}\right)^2 = 5 \times 9 = 45\text{ minutes}$.

questions.original_text: If a circular ultrasound transducer of radius a = 8 mm operating at a central frequency of 1 MHz has a pressure beam pattern in a medium as given below: P(r, 0) \propto \sin(k a^2 / 4r). Here, k is the wave number, r is the axial distance from the transducer center. The speed of sound in the medium is 1600 m s^-1. The reduction in intensity between r = 8 cm and r = 16 cm is ________ dB. Give your answer as a positive quantity rounded off to two decimal places.
questions.display_text:
If a circular ultrasound transducer of radius $a = 8\text{ mm}$ operating at a central frequency of $1\text{ MHz}$ has a pressure beam pattern in a medium as given below:
$$P(r, 0) \propto \sin\left(\frac{ka^2}{4r}\right)$$
Here, $k$ is the wave number, $r$ is the axial distance from the transducer center. The speed of sound in the medium is $1600\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

The reduction in intensity between $r = 8\text{ cm}$ and $r = 16\text{ cm}$ is ________ $\text{dB}$. Give your answer as a positive quantity rounded off to two decimal places.

explanation.text: The wavelength is $\lambda = \frac{c}{f} = \frac{1600\text{ m/s}}{10^6\text{ Hz}} = 1.6\text{ mm}$, and the wavenumber is $k = \frac{2\pi}{\lambda} = \frac{2\pi}{1.6\text{ mm}}$. Given $a = 8\text{ mm}$, we compute $\frac{ka^2}{4} = \frac{2\pi (64\text{ mm}^2)}{4(1.6\text{ mm})} = 20\pi\text{ mm} = 2\pi\text{ cm}$. At $r_1 = 8\text{ cm}$, the argument is $\frac{2\pi}{8} = \frac{\pi}{4}$, so $P(r_1, 0) \propto \sin\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$. At $r_2 = 16\text{ cm}$, the argument is $\frac{2\pi}{16} = \frac{\pi}{8}$, so $P(r_2, 0) \propto \sin\left(\frac{\pi}{8}\right) \approx 0.38268$. Since acoustic intensity is proportional to pressure squared ($I \propto P^2$), the reduction in intensity in dB is $20\log_{10}\left(\frac{P(r_1, 0)}{P(r_2, 0)}\right) = 20\log_{10}\left(\frac{0.70711}{0.38268}\right) = 20\log_{10}(1.84776) \approx 5.333\text{ dB} \approx 5.33\text{ dB}$.

questions.original_text: The source in the figure is a current source and the circuit is in steady state. At t = 1.57 seconds, the value of v in the circuit given below is ________ volts. Give your answer rounded off to two decimal places.
questions.display_text: The source in the figure is a current source and the circuit is in steady state. At $t = 1.57\text{ seconds}$, the value of $v$ in the circuit given below is ________ volts. Give your answer rounded off to two decimal places.

explanation.text: The current source $I = \sin(t)\text{ A}$ operates at angular frequency $\omega = 1\text{ rad/s}$. The parallel $1\text{ H}$ inductor and $1\text{ F}$ capacitor are at parallel resonance since $\omega_0 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}} = 1\text{ rad/s}$, so their combined admittance is $Y_{LC} = j\omega C + \frac{1}{j\omega L} = j1 - j1 = 0$ (an open circuit). Therefore, the entire source current $\sin(t)$ flows through the $2\text{ }\Omega$ resistor, giving $v(t) = 2\sin(t)\text{ V}$. Note that at $t = \frac{\pi}{2} \approx 1.57\text{ s}$ (partially cropped as '0.57' or '1.57' on the left margin of Page 33), $v(1.57) = 2\sin(1.57) \approx 2.00\text{ V}$.

questions.original_text: The equivalent impedance, Z_AB, in the circuit given below is ________ Ohm. Give your answer rounded off to one decimal place.
questions.display_text: The equivalent impedance, $Z_{AB}$, in the circuit given below is ________ $\Omega$. Give your answer rounded off to one decimal place.

explanation.text: Apply a test voltage $V_{\text{test}}$ at terminals AB with input current $I_{\text{test}}$. The voltage at the central node above the vertical $1\text{ }\Omega$ resistor is $V$. Since the dependent voltage source on the left also has voltage $V$, the potential difference across the top-left $1\text{ }\Omega$ resistor is $V - V = 0\text{ V}$, meaning zero current flows into the left branch! Consequently, all of $I_{\text{test}}$ flows through the top-right $1\text{ }\Omega$ resistor and down through the vertical $1\text{ }\Omega$ resistor in series. Thus, $Z_{AB} = 1\text{ }\Omega + 1\text{ }\Omega = 2.0\text{ }\Omega$.

questions.original_text: The bandwidth of ECG signal ranges from 0.5 Hz to 100 Hz. If a single ADC is used to digitize data from 8 ECG channels then the minimum ADC sampling rate is ________ Hz. Give your answer rounded off to the nearest integer.
questions.display_text: The bandwidth of ECG signal ranges from $0.5\text{ Hz}$ to $100\text{ Hz}$. If a single ADC is used to digitize data from $8$ ECG channels then the minimum ADC sampling rate is ________ $\text{Hz}$. Give your answer rounded off to the nearest integer.

explanation.text: The maximum frequency of each ECG channel is $f_{\max} = 100\text{ Hz}$, so the minimum Nyquist sampling rate per channel is $f_{s,\text{channel}} = 2 f_{\max} = 200\text{ Hz}$. For $8$ time-division multiplexed channels digitized by a single ADC, the minimum total ADC sampling rate is $8 \times 200\text{ Hz} = 1600\text{ Hz}$.

questions.original_text: If x[n] = u[n] - u[n-5], and h[n] = \delta[n] - \delta[n-1] and y[n] = x[n] * h[n], then the value of \sum_{n=-\infty}^{\infty} y[n] is ________. Give your answer rounded off to the nearest integer.
questions.display_text: If $x[n] = u[n] - u[n-5]$, and $h[n] = \delta[n] - \delta[n-1]$ and $y[n] = x[n] * h[n]$, then the value of $\sum_{n=-\infty}^{\infty} y[n]$ is ________. Give your answer rounded off to the nearest integer.

explanation.text: By the sum property of discrete-time convolution, $\sum_{n=-\infty}^{\infty} y[n] = \left(\sum_{n=-\infty}^{\infty} x[n]\right)\left(\sum_{n=-\infty}^{\infty} h[n]\right)$. Since $\sum_{n=-\infty}^{\infty} h[n] = 1 - 1 = 0$, the sum of $y[n]$ over all $n$ is $5 \times 0 = 0$.

questions.original_text: In the figure below, the diode is ideal. The current reading shown in the ammeter is ________ A. Give your answer rounded off to the nearest integer.
questions.display_text: In the figure below, the diode is ideal. The current reading shown in the ammeter is ________ $\text{A}$. Give your answer rounded off to the nearest integer.

explanation.text: The source is $V_s = \sin(t)\text{ V}$ with $\omega = 1\text{ rad/s}$. In the AC bridge, the four arm impedances at $\omega = 1\text{ rad/s}$ are: top-left $Z_1 = j\omega L = j1\text{ }\Omega$, bottom-left $Z_2 = 1\text{ }\Omega$, top-right $Z_3 = 1\text{ }\Omega$, and bottom-right $Z_4 = \frac{1}{j\omega C} = -j1\text{ }\Omega$. Checking the bridge balance condition: $Z_1 Z_4 = (j1)(-j1) = 1$ and $Z_2 Z_3 = (1)(1) = 1$. Since $Z_1 Z_4 = Z_2 Z_3$, the bridge is completely balanced at $\omega = 1\text{ rad/s}$, so the potential difference across the central detector branch is identically zero at all times, and the ammeter reads $0\text{ A}$.

questions.original_text: In the figure below, the Fourier series of v(t), in volts, is given as: v(t) = v_0 + 2 cos(omega_0 t) + 5 cos(3 omega_0 t) + cos(5 omega_0 t). The capacitor is a short circuit for all AC signals. The power absorbed by the 1 Ohm resistor is ________ W. Give your answer rounded off to the nearest integer.
questions.display_text:
In the figure below, the Fourier series of $v(t)$, in volts, is given as:
$$v(t) = v_0 + 2\cos(\omega_0 t) + 5\cos(3\omega_0 t) + \cos(5\omega_0 t)$$
The capacitor is a short circuit for all AC signals. The power absorbed by the $1\text{ }\Omega$ resistor is ________ $\text{W}$. Give your answer rounded off to the nearest integer.

explanation.text: The series blocking capacitor blocks the DC component $v_0$ (acting as an open circuit at DC) and acts as a short circuit for all AC harmonics. Thus, the voltage across the $R = 1\text{ }\Omega$ resistor is $v_R(t) = 2\cos(\omega_0 t) + 5\cos(3\omega_0 t) + \cos(5\omega_0 t)$. By Parseval's relation, the average power absorbed by the $1\text{ }\Omega$ resistor is $P = \frac{V_{\text{rms,AC}}^2}{R} = \frac{1}{1\text{ }\Omega} \left(\frac{2^2}{2} + \frac{5^2}{2} + \frac{1^2}{2}\right) = \frac{4 + 25 + 1}{2} = \frac{30}{2} = 15\text{ W}$.

questions.original_text: An artificial fore-arm has a moment-of-inertia around the center of mass as 0.3 kg.m^2. The mass of the artificial fore-arm is 3 kg. If the distance from the elbow joint to the center of mass of the fore-arm is 20 cm, the moment-of-inertia of the fore-arm about the elbow joint is ________ kg.m^2. Give your answer rounded off to two decimal places.
questions.display_text: An artificial fore-arm has a moment-of-inertia around the center of mass as $0.3\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m}^2$. The mass of the artificial fore-arm is $3\text{ kg}$. If the distance from the elbow joint to the center of mass of the fore-arm is $20\text{ cm}$, the moment-of-inertia of the fore-arm about the elbow joint is ________ $\text{kg}\cdot\text{m}^2$. Give your answer rounded off to two decimal places.

explanation.text: By the Parallel Axis Theorem, the moment of inertia about the elbow joint is $I_{\text{elbow}} = I_{\text{CM}} + m d^2$. Substituting $I_{\text{CM}} = 0.3\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m}^2$, $m = 3\text{ kg}$, and $d = 20\text{ cm} = 0.2\text{ m}$ gives $I_{\text{elbow}} = 0.3 + 3(0.2)^2 = 0.3 + 0.12 = 0.42\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m}^2$.

questions.original_text: A bio-potential signal of 4 mV on the skin surface was fed to an amplifier with a differential gain of 2000. The noise in the signal is 1000 mV. If the amplifier output produces a noise output of 200 mV, the common mode rejection ratio of the amplifier is ________ dB. Give your answer rounded to the nearest integer.
questions.display_text: A bio-potential signal of $4\text{ mV}$ on the skin surface was fed to an amplifier with a differential gain of $2000$. The noise in the signal is $1000\text{ mV}$. If the amplifier output produces a noise output of $200\text{ mV}$, the common mode rejection ratio of the amplifier is ________ $\text{dB}$. Give your answer rounded to the nearest integer.

explanation.text: The common-mode gain is $A_{\text{cm}} = \frac{V_{\text{noise,out}}}{V_{\text{noise,in}}} = \frac{200\text{ mV}}{1000\text{ mV}} = 0.2$. Given the differential gain $A_d = 2000$, the Common Mode Rejection Ratio is $\text{CMRR} = \frac{A_d}{A_{\text{cm}}} = \frac{2000}{0.2} = 10^4$. Expressed in decibels: $\text{CMRR}_{\text{dB}} = 20\log_{10}(10^4) = 80\text{ dB}$.

questions.original_text: In a motor nerve conduction velocity experiment, the distance between the distal and the recording sites is 4 cm and the distance between the proximal and the recording sites is 24 cm. The distal and proximal latencies were recorded as 6 ms and 10 ms, respectively. The nerve conduction velocity is ________ meters per second. Give your answer rounded off to the nearest integer.
questions.display_text: In a motor nerve conduction velocity experiment, the distance between the distal and the recording sites is $4\text{ cm}$ and the distance between the proximal and the recording sites is $24\text{ cm}$. The distal and proximal latencies were recorded as $6\text{ ms}$ and $10\text{ ms}$, respectively. The nerve conduction velocity is ________ meters per second. Give your answer rounded off to the nearest integer.

explanation.text: Nerve conduction velocity (NCV) is calculated from the difference in distance divided by the difference in latency between proximal and distal stimulation sites (eliminating neuromuscular junction delay): $\text{NCV} = \frac{d_{\text{proximal}} - d_{\text{distal}}}{t_{\text{proximal}} - t_{\text{distal}}} = \frac{24\text{ cm} - 4\text{ cm}}{10\text{ ms} - 6\text{ ms}} = \frac{0.20\text{ m}}{4 \times 10^{-3}\text{ s}} = 50\text{ m/s}$.

questions.original_text: A person creates an apparatus as shown in the figure to exercise the extensor muscle of the hand. It is given that OP = 0.15 m, OQ = 0.35 m, theta = 30 degrees, the weight of the lower arm = 20 N, the center of mass of the lower arm is at point P, the magnitude of the applied tensile force F = 50 N. If the extensor muscle is acting with a moment arm of 0.25 m, the muscle force required to hold the hand at the position shown in the figure is ________ N. Give your answer rounded off to the nearest integer.
questions.display_text: A person creates an apparatus as shown in the figure to exercise the extensor muscle of the hand. It is given that $OP = 0.15\text{ m}$, $OQ = 0.35\text{ m}$, $\theta = 30^\circ$, the weight of the lower arm $= 20\text{ N}$, the center of mass of the lower arm is at point $P$, the magnitude of the applied tensile force $F = 50\text{ N}$. If the extensor muscle is acting with a moment arm of $0.25\text{ m}$, the muscle force required to hold the hand at the position shown in the figure is ________ $\text{N}$. Give your answer rounded off to the nearest integer.

explanation.text: Taking the sum of moments about the elbow joint $O$ in static equilibrium ($\sum M_O = 0$): the upward vertical component of the cable tension at $Q$ ($OQ = 0.35\text{ m}$) is $F\sin 30^\circ = 50 \times 0.5 = 25\text{ N}$, producing a counterclockwise (flexion) moment of $25\text{ N} \times 0.35\text{ m} = 8.75\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}$. The weight of the lower arm ($W = 20\text{ N}$ at $OP = 0.15\text{ m}$) acts downward, producing a clockwise moment of $20\text{ N} \times 0.15\text{ m} = 3.00\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}$. To balance the net counterclockwise moment of $8.75 - 3.00 = 5.75\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}$, the extensor muscle (moment arm $d_m = 0.25\text{ m}$) must exert a force $F_m = \frac{5.75\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}}{0.25\text{ m}} = 23\text{ N}$.

questions.original_text: Here are two analogous groups, Group-I and Group-II, that list words in their decreasing order of intensity. Identify the missing word in Group-II. Group-I: Abuse -> Insult -> Ridicule Group-II: ________ -> Praise -> Appreciate
questions.display_text:
Here are two analogous groups, Group-I and Group-II, that list words in their decreasing order of intensity. Identify the missing word in Group-II.

Group-I: $\text{Abuse} \rightarrow \text{Insult} \rightarrow \text{Ridicule}$

Group-II: $\underline{\hspace{2cm}} \rightarrow \text{Praise} \rightarrow \text{Appreciate}$

questions.original_text: Had I learnt acting as a child, I ________ a famous film star. Select the most appropriate option to complete the above sentence.
questions.display_text:
Had I learnt acting as a child, I ________ a famous film star.

Select the most appropriate option to complete the above sentence.

explanation.text: The clause 'Had I learnt acting as a child' is an inverted third-conditional antecedent (equivalent to 'If I had learnt acting as a child') referring to an unreal past condition. The main clause requires a modal perfect construction ('could have been' / 'would have been').

questions.original_text: The 12 musical notes are given as C, C#, D, D#, E, F, F#, G, G#, A, A#, and B. Frequency of each note is 2^(1/12) times the frequency of the previous note. If the frequency of the note C is 130.8 Hz, then the ratio of frequencies of notes F# and C is:
questions.display_text: The 12 musical notes are given as $\text{C}, \text{C}^\#, \text{D}, \text{D}^\#, \text{E}, \text{F}, \text{F}^\#, \text{G}, \text{G}^\#, \text{A}, \text{A}^\#,$ and $\text{B}$. Frequency of each note is $\sqrt[12]{2}$ times the frequency of the previous note. If the frequency of the note $\text{C}$ is $130.8\text{ Hz}$, then the ratio of frequencies of notes $\text{F}^\#$ and $\text{C}$ is:

explanation.text: Counting steps from $\text{C}$ (index 0): $\text{C}^\#$ (1), $\text{D}$ (2), $\text{D}^\#$ (3), $\text{E}$ (4), $\text{F}$ (5), $\text{F}^\#$ (6). Since $\text{F}^\#$ is 6 semitones above $\text{C}$, the ratio of their frequencies is $(\sqrt[12]{2})^6 = 2^{6/12} = 2^{1/2} = \sqrt{2}$.

questions.original_text: The following figures show three curves generated using an iterative algorithm. The total length of the curve generated after 'Iteration n' is: Note: The figures shown are representative. Iteration 0: 1; Iteration 1: Length of each segment: 1/3; Iteration 2: Length of each segment: 1/9
questions.display_text:
The following figures show three curves generated using an iterative algorithm. The total length of the curve generated after 'Iteration $n$' is:

Note: The figures shown are representative.

explanation.text: At Iteration 0, the curve consists of 1 segment of length $1$, so total length $L_0 = 1$. At Iteration 1, the segment is replaced by 5 segments each of length $\frac{1}{3}$, giving total length $L_1 = \frac{5}{3}$. questions.original_text: Which one of the following plots represents f(x) = -|x|/x, where x is a non-zero real number? Note: The figures shown are representative.
questions.display_text:
Which one of the following plots represents $f(x) = -\frac{|x|}{x}$, where $x$ is a non-zero real number?

Note: The figures shown are representative.

explanation.text: For $x > 0$, $|x| = x$, so $f(x) = -\frac{x}{x} = -1$. For $x < 0$, $|x| = -x$, so $f(x) = -\frac{-x}{x} = +1$. Thus, the graph is a horizontal line at $f(x) = +1$ in the second quadrant ($x < 0$) and a horizontal line at $f(x) = -1$ in the fourth quadrant ($x > 0$), which matches plot (A).

questions.original_text: Identify the option that has the most appropriate sequence such that a coherent paragraph is formed: P. Over time, such adaptations lead to significant evolutionary changes with the potential to shape the development of new species. Q. In natural world, organisms constantly adapt to their environments in response to challenges and opportunities. R. This process of adaptation is driven by the principle of natural selection, where favorable traits increase an organism's chances of survival and reproduction. S. As environments change, organisms that can adapt their behavior, structure and physiology to such changes are more likely to survive.
questions.display_text:
Identify the option that has the most appropriate sequence such that a coherent paragraph is formed:

P. Over time, such adaptations lead to significant evolutionary changes with the potential to shape the development of new species.
Q. In natural world, organisms constantly adapt to their environments in response to challenges and opportunities.
R. This process of adaptation is driven by the principle of natural selection, where favorable traits increase an organism's chances of survival and reproduction.
S. As environments change, organisms that can adapt their behavior, structure and physiology to such changes are more likely to survive.

explanation.text: Sentence Q introduces the general theme of organisms adapting to their environments. Sentence S elaborates on how changing environments favor adaptable organisms. Sentence R explains the mechanism behind 'This process of adaptation' (natural selection). Finally, sentence P concludes with the long-term macroevolutionary outcome ('Over time, such adaptations lead to... new species'). Thus, $Q \rightarrow S \rightarrow R \rightarrow P$ forms a coherent paragraph.

questions.original_text: A stick of length one meter is broken at two locations at distances of b1 and b2 from the origin (0), as shown in the figure. Note that 0 < b1 < b2 < 1. Which one of the following is NOT a necessary condition for forming a triangle using the three pieces? Note: All lengths are in meter. The figure shown is representative.
questions.display_text:
A stick of length one meter is broken at two locations at distances of $b_1$ and $b_2$ from the origin ($0$), as shown in the figure. Note that $0 < b_1 < b_2 < 1$. Which one of the following is NOT a necessary condition for forming a triangle using the three pieces?

Note: All lengths are in meter. The figure shown is representative.

explanation.text: The lengths of the three pieces are $L_1 = b_1$, $L_2 = b_2 - b_1$, and $L_3 = 1 - b_2$, with $L_1 + L_2 + L_3 = 1$. By the triangle inequality, the length of each piece must be strictly less than half the total perimeter ($0.5$): (1) $b_1 < 0.5$ (Option A); (2) $1 - b_2 < 0.5 \implies b_2 > 0.5$ (Option B); (3) $b_2 - b_1 < 0.5 \implies b_2 < b_1 + 0.5$ (Option C). However, $b_1 + b_2 < 1$ is NOT necessary (for example, $b_1 = 0.4, b_2 = 0.7$ gives side lengths $0.4, 0.3, 0.3$ which form an isosceles triangle, yet $b_1 + b_2 = 1.1 > 1$).

questions.original_text: The table lists the top 5 nations according to the number of gold medals won in a tournament; also included are the number of silver and the bronze medals won by them. Based only on the data provided in the table, which one of the following statements is INCORRECT? [USA: 40, 44, 41; Canada: 39, 27, 24; Japan: 20, 12, 13; Australia: 19, 17, 16; France: 16, 26, 22]
questions.display_text:
The table lists the top 5 nations according to the number of gold medals won in a tournament; also included are the number of silver and the bronze medals won by them. Based only on the data provided in the table, which one of the following statements is INCORRECT?

| Nation | Gold | Silver | Bronze |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| USA | 40 | 44 | 41 |
| Canada | 39 | 27 | 24 |
| Japan | 20 | 12 | 13 |
| Australia | 19 | 17 | 16 |
| France | 16 | 26 | 22 |
options: France will occupy the third place if the list were made on the basis of the total number of medals won.
The order of the top two nations will not change even if the list is made on the basis of the total number of medals won.
USA and Canada together have less than 50% of the medals awarded to the nations in the above table.
Canada has won twice as many total medals as Japan.

explanation.text: Calculating the total medals for each nation: USA $= 40 + 44 + 41 = 125$; Canada $= 39 + 27 + 24 = 90$; Japan $= 20 + 12 + 13 = 45$; Australia $= 19 + 17 + 16 = 52$; France $= 16 + 26 + 22 = 64$. Total medals across all 5 nations $= 125 + 90 + 45 + 52 + 64 = 376$. USA and Canada together have $125 + 90 = 215$ medals, which is $\frac{215}{376} \approx 57.18\%$ (more than $50\%$). Therefore, statement (C) is INCORRECT.

questions.original_text: An organization allows its employees to work independently on consultancy projects but charges an overhead on the consulting fee. The overhead is 20% of the consulting fee, if the fee is up to Rs. 5,00,000. For higher fees, the overhead is Rs. 1,00,000 plus 10% of the amount by which the fee exceeds Rs. 5,00,000. The government charges a Goods and Services Tax of 18% on the total amount (the consulting fee plus the overhead). An employee of the organization charges this entire amount, i.e., the consulting fee, overhead, and tax, to the client. If the client cannot pay more than Rs. 10,00,000, what is the maximum consulting fee that the employee can charge?
questions.display_text: An organization allows its employees to work independently on consultancy projects but charges an overhead on the consulting fee. The overhead is $20\%$ of the consulting fee, if the fee is up to ₹ $5,00,000$. For higher fees, the overhead is ₹ $1,00,000$ plus $10\%$ of the amount by which the fee exceeds ₹ $5,00,000$. The government charges a Goods and Services Tax of $18\%$ on the total amount (the consulting fee plus the overhead). An employee of the organization charges this entire amount, i.e., the consulting fee, overhead, and tax, to the client. If the client cannot pay more than ₹ $10,00,000$, what is the maximum consulting fee that the employee can charge?

explanation.text: Let the consulting fee be $x > 5,00,000$. The overhead is $1,00,000 + 0.10(x - 5,00,000) = 50,000 + 0.1x$. The total amount before tax is $x + (50,000 + 0.1x) = 1.1x + 50,000$. Including $18\%$ GST, the total amount billed to the client is $1.18(1.1x + 50,000) = 10,00,000$. Solving for $x$: $1.1x + 50,000 = \frac{10,00,000}{1.18} \approx 8,47,457.63 \implies 1.1x = 7,97,457.63 \implies x \approx 7,24,961.48 \approx \text{₹ } 7,24,961$.

questions.original_text: The determinant of a 3 x 3 matrix M is 8. If every element of M is multiplied by -2, the determinant of the modified matrix will be ________.

questions.original_text: The closed loop system shown below [unity negative feedback with G(s) = 25 / (s(s+5))]
questions.display_text: The closed loop system shown below with open-loop transfer function $G(s) = \frac{25}{s(s+5)}$ and unity negative feedback

explanation.text: The characteristic equation of the unity negative feedback system is $1 + G(s) = 0 \implies s(s + 5) + 25 = s^2 + 5s + 25 = 0$. Comparing with the standard second-order form $s^2 + 2\zeta\omega_n s + \omega_n^2 = 0$, we have $\omega_n = \sqrt{25} = 5\text{ rad/s}$ and $2\zeta\omega_n = 5 \implies \zeta = \frac{5}{2 \times 5} = 0.5$. Since $0 < \zeta < 1$, the closed-loop system is underdamped.

questions.original_text: Let R1, R2 and R3 be the Reynolds numbers corresponding to the following three cases, respectively: Case 1: A 1 um long bacterium swimming in water Case 2: A 10 cm long fish swimming in water Case 3: A 10 m long whale swimming in water. If each of them covers a distance equal to their respective body length in one second, which one of the following is CORRECT?
questions.display_text:
Let $R_1$, $R_2$ and $R_3$ be the Reynolds numbers corresponding to the following three cases, respectively:

* **Case 1:** A $1\text{ }\mu\text{m}$ long bacterium swimming in water
* **Case 2:** A $10\text{ cm}$ long fish swimming in water
* **Case 3:** A $10\text{ m}$ long whale swimming in water

If each of them covers a distance equal to their respective body length in one second, which one of the following is CORRECT?

explanation.text: The Reynolds number is $R = \frac{\rho v L}{\mu}$. Since each organism travels its body length $L$ in $1\text{ s}$, its speed is $v = L / (1\text{ s})$, so $R \propto L^2$. Because $L_1 = 10^{-6}\text{ m} < L_2 = 10^{-1}\text{ m} < L_3 = 10\text{ m}$, we have $R_1 < R_2 < R_3$.

questions.original_text: The shape of an elastic rod of length l is represented by the position vector r(s) corresponding to the arc length s. If the bending energy of the rod is E = K \int_0^l (\partial^2 r / \partial s^2)^2 ds, what is the dimension of K in terms of mass M, length L and time T?
questions.display_text:
The shape of an elastic rod of length $l$ is represented by the position vector $\vec{r}(s)$ corresponding to the arc length $s$. If the bending energy of the rod is
$$E = K \int_0^l \left(\frac{\partial^2 \vec{r}}{\partial s^2}\right)^2 ds,$$
what is the dimension of $K$ in terms of mass $M$, length $L$ and time $T$?

explanation.text: Both $\vec{r}$ and $s$ have dimensions of length ($L$), so curvature $\frac{\partial^2 \vec{r}}{\partial s^2}$ has dimension $\frac{L}{L^2} = L^{-1}$. The integral $\int_0^l \left(\frac{\partial^2 \vec{r}}{\partial s^2}\right)^2 ds$ has dimension $(L^{-1})^2 \cdot L = L^{-1}$. Since energy $E$ has dimension $ML^2T^{-2}$, the bending rigidity $K$ has dimension $[K] = \frac{[E]}{L^{-1}} = ML^3T^{-2}$.

questions.original_text: The elements of the dataset {-5, 1, a, 5, b} are in ascending order. If both mean and median of the dataset are equal to 3, what is the value of b?

questions.original_text: The Electroencephalogram (EEG) voltage measured by a test device is 2.4 uV, while the reference device measured it to be 3.0 uV. What is the percentage error of the test device?
questions.display_text: The Electroencephalogram (EEG) voltage measured by a test device is $2.4\text{ }\mu\text{V}$, while the reference device measured it to be $3.0\text{ }\mu\text{V}$. What is the percentage error of the test device?

explanation.text: Percentage error relative to the reference (true) value is $\frac{|V_{\text{test}} - V_{\text{ref}}|}{V_{\text{ref}}} \times 100\% = \frac{|2.4 - 3.0|}{3.0} \times 100\% = \frac{0.6}{3.0} \times 100\% = 20\%$.

questions.original_text: A time domain signal is given by x(t) = 20 sin(100 pi t) + 36 sin(150 pi t) - 2 sin(300 pi t), where time t is in seconds. Among the following options, what is the frequency (in Hz) at which x(t) should be sampled for accurate signal reconstruction?
questions.display_text:
A time domain signal is given by
$$x(t) = 20\sin(100\pi t) + 36\sin(150\pi t) - 2\sin(300\pi t),$$
where time $t$ is in seconds. Among the following options, what is the frequency (in Hz) at which $x(t)$ should be sampled for accurate signal reconstruction?

explanation.text: The frequencies of the three sinusoidal components are $f_1 = \frac{100\pi}{2\pi} = 50\text{ Hz}$, $f_2 = \frac{150\pi}{2\pi} = 75\text{ Hz}$, and $f_3 = \frac{300\pi}{2\pi} = 150\text{ Hz}$. The maximum frequency present in $x(t)$ is $f_{\max} = 150\text{ Hz}$. By the Nyquist-Shannon sampling theorem, accurate reconstruction requires a sampling frequency $f_s > 2f_{\max} = 300\text{ Hz}$. Among the given options, only $500\text{ Hz}$ satisfies $f_s > 300\text{ Hz}$.

questions.original_text: A voltage source Vs = 5 sin(100t + pi/2) volts is driving a current I = 10 sin(100t + pi/6) mA through a circuit. The average power dissipated in the circuit is ________ mW.
questions.display_text:
A voltage source $V_s = 5\sin\left(100t + \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\text{ volts}$ is driving a current $I = 10\sin\left(100t + \frac{\pi}{6}\right)\text{ mA}$ through a circuit.

The average power dissipated in the circuit is ________ $\text{mW}$.

explanation.text: The average power dissipated in an AC circuit is $P_{\text{avg}} = \frac{1}{2} V_m I_m \cos(\theta_v - \theta_i)$. Substituting $V_m = 5\text{ V}$, $I_m = 10\text{ mA}$, and $\theta_v - \theta_i = \frac{\pi}{2} - \frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{\pi}{3}$ gives $P_{\text{avg}} = \frac{1}{2} (5)(10) \cos\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right) = 25 \times 0.5 = 12.5\text{ mW}$.

questions.original_text: N independent trials of a binomial random variable yield an expectation value of 16 and variance of 12. What is the value of N?
questions.display_text: $N$ independent trials of a binomial random variable yield an expectation value of $16$ and variance of $12$. What is the value of $N$?

explanation.text: For a binomial distribution $B(N, p)$, the mean is $\mu = Np = 16$ and the variance is $\sigma^2 = Np(1 - p) = 12$. Dividing the variance by the mean gives $1 - p = \frac{12}{16} = \frac{3}{4} \implies p = \frac{1}{4}$. Substituting $p = \frac{1}{4}$ into $Np = 16$ yields $N = 16 \times 4 = 64$.

questions.original_text: Given a function y(x) satisfying the differential equation y'' - 0.25y = 0, with initial conditions y(0) = 1; y'(0) = 1, what is the value of y(log_e 100)? Here, y' and y'' are the first and second derivatives of y, respectively.
questions.display_text:
Given a function $y(x)$ satisfying the differential equation
$$y'' - 0.25y = 0,$$
with initial conditions $y(0) = 1$; $y'(0) = 1$, what is the value of $y(\log_e 100)$?

Here, $y'$ and $y''$ are the first and second derivatives of $y$, respectively.

explanation.text: The auxiliary equation is $r^2 - 0.25 = 0 \implies r = \pm 0.5$. The general solution is $y(x) = C_1 e^{0.5x} + C_2 e^{-0.5x}$, with derivative $y'(x) = 0.5 C_1 e^{0.5x} - 0.5 C_2 e^{-0.5x}$. Applying the initial conditions at $x = 0$: $C_1 + C_2 = 1$ and $0.5(C_1 - C_2) = 1 \implies C_1 - C_2 = 2$. Solving gives $C_1 = 1.5$ and $C_2 = -0.5$. Evaluating at $x = \ln 100$: since $e^{0.5 \ln 100} = 100^{0.5} = 10$ and $e^{-0.5 \ln 100} = 10^{-1} = 0.1$, we get $y(\ln 100) = 1.5(10) - 0.5(0.1) = 15 - 0.05 = 14.95$.

questions.original_text: In the circuit shown below, Vin = 10 cos(1000t) volts. The magnitude of the input impedance of the circuit is ________ kOhm. (rounded off to one decimal place)
questions.display_text: In the circuit shown below, $V_{\text{in}} = 10\cos(1000t)\text{ volts}$. The magnitude of the input impedance of the circuit is ________ $\text{k}\Omega$. (rounded off to one decimal place)

explanation.text: The circuit consists of a $3\text{ k}\Omega$ resistor in series with the parallel combination of a $1\text{ k}\Omega$ resistor and a $1\text{ }\mu\text{F}$ capacitor. At $\omega = 1000\text{ rad/s}$, the capacitive impedance is $Z_C = \frac{1}{j\omega C} = \frac{1}{j(1000)(10^{-6})} = -j1000\text{ }\Omega = -j1\text{ k}\Omega$. The parallel impedance of $1\text{ k}\Omega$ and $-j1\text{ k}\Omega$ is $Z_p = \frac{1(-j1)}{1 - j1} = \frac{-j(1 + j)}{2} = 0.5 - j0.5\text{ k}\Omega$. Adding the series $3\text{ k}\Omega$ resistor gives $Z_{\text{in}} = 3 + 0.5 - j0.5 = 3.5 - j0.5\text{ k}\Omega$. Its magnitude is $|Z_{\text{in}}| = \sqrt{3.5^2 + (-0.5)^2} = \sqrt{12.25 + 0.25} = \sqrt{12.5} \approx 3.536\text{ k}\Omega \approx 3.5\text{ k}\Omega$.

questions.original_text: Gelatin solutions P and Q of concentrations 3.5% and 0.5%, respectively, need to be mixed to obtain a 3% solution R. How much volume (in ml) of P needs to be mixed with 100 ml of Q to obtain R? (Choose the correct option) All concentrations are in units of weight/volume.
questions.display_text:
Gelatin solutions P and Q of concentrations $3.5\%$ and $0.5\%$, respectively, need to be mixed to obtain a $3\%$ solution R. How much volume (in mL) of P needs to be mixed with $100\text{ mL}$ of Q to obtain R? (Choose the correct option)

All concentrations are in units of weight/volume.

explanation.text: By mass balance of gelatin: $C_P V_P + C_Q V_Q = C_R (V_P + V_Q)$. Substituting $C_P = 3.5$, $C_Q = 0.5$, $V_Q = 100\text{ mL}$, and $C_R = 3.0$: $3.5 V_P + 0.5(100) = 3.0(V_P + 100) \implies 0.5 V_P = 300 - 50 = 250 \implies V_P = 500\text{ mL}$.

questions.original_text: Which of the following is/are CORRECT about the value of y = log_e(-e^x), where x is a real number.
questions.display_text: Which of the following is/are CORRECT about the value of $y = \log_e(-e^x)$, where $x$ is a real number?
options: $y = x \pm i n\pi$, where $n$ is an odd integer and $i = \sqrt{-1}$
$y = x \pm i n\pi$, where $n$ is an even integer and $i = \sqrt{-1}$

explanation.text: Since $x$ is real, $e^x > 0$ and $-e^x < 0$. In the complex plane, $-1 = e^{\pm i n\pi}$ for any odd integer $n$. Therefore, the complex logarithm is $y = \ln(-e^x) = \ln(e^x \cdot e^{\pm i n\pi}) = x \pm i n\pi$, where $n$ is an odd integer. Thus, $y$ is complex-valued (B) and given by $x \pm i n\pi$ for odd integers $n$ (C).

The transmission coefficient is independent of the impedance of biological tissues

explanation.text: Specific acoustic impedance is defined as $Z = \rho c$, which is directly proportional to tissue density $\rho$ (Option A). At an interface between two tissues with impedances $Z_1$ and $Z_2$, the amplitude reflection coefficient $R = \frac{Z_2 - Z_1}{Z_2 + Z_1}$ depends directly on the acoustic impedance mismatch (Option B).

questions.original_text: Two systems U and V are defined as shown below. Which of the following statement(s) is/are CORRECT? System U: x(t) -> y(t) = x(t)^2 + 1; System V: x(t) -> y(t) = x(t+1)
questions.display_text:
Two systems U and V are defined as shown below. Which of the following statement(s) is/are CORRECT?

* **System U:** $x(t) \longrightarrow y(t) = x(t)^2 + 1$
* **System V:** $x(t) \longrightarrow y(t) = x(t+1)$
options: System U is nonlinear; System V is linear
System U is causal; System V is noncausal
System U is noncausal; System V is causal
System U is nonlinear; System V is nonlinear

explanation.text: System U ($y(t) = x(t)^2 + 1$) violates both homogeneity and additivity (and does not map zero input to zero output), so it is **nonlinear**; since $y(t)$ depends only on the present input $x(t)$, it is memoryless and therefore **causal**. System V ($y(t) = x(t+1)$) is a pure time-advance operator, which satisfies superposition and is **linear**, but because $y(t)$ depends on a future input value $x(t+1)$, it is **noncausal**. Thus, both (A) and (B) are correct.

questions.original_text: Which of the following statement(s) about pulse oximetry is/are TRUE?
questions.display_text: Which of the following statement(s) about pulse oximetry is/are TRUE?
options: Oxygenated hemoglobin absorbs less infrared light (900 nm) compared to deoxygenated hemoglobin
Oxygenated hemoglobin absorbs less visible light (600 nm) compared to deoxygenated hemoglobin
Oxygenated hemoglobin absorbs more visible light (600 nm) compared to deoxygenated hemoglobin
Oxygenated hemoglobin absorbs more infrared light (900 nm) compared to deoxygenated hemoglobin

explanation.text: Pulse oximetry relies on the differential absorption spectra of $\text{HbO}_2$ and $\text{Hb}$ on opposite sides of their isosbestic point (~805 nm): in the visible red region (~600–660 nm), oxygenated hemoglobin ($\text{HbO}_2$) absorbs **less** light than deoxygenated hemoglobin ($\text{Hb}$) (Option B), whereas in the near-infrared region (~900–940 nm), $\text{HbO}_2$ absorbs **more** light than $\text{Hb}$ (Option D).

questions.original_text: Which of the following statement(s) is/are CORRECT about neuronal membrane and neuronal action potential?
questions.display_text: Which of the following statement(s) is/are CORRECT about neuronal membrane and neuronal action potential?
options: Application of an outward current depolarizes the neuronal membrane
Application of an inward current depolarizes the neuronal membrane
Increasing the stimulus strength increases the amplitude of neuronal action potential
Increasing the stimulus strength decreases the latency of neuronal action potential

explanation.text: An inward current (flow of positive ions into the cell) makes the intracellular potential less negative, thereby depolarizing the neuronal membrane (Option B). Because action potentials obey the all-or-none law, suprathreshold stimulus strength does not increase action potential amplitude (C is false), but a stronger suprathreshold current charges the membrane capacitance to threshold faster, decreasing the latency to action potential onset (Option D).

questions.original_text: A discrete linear time invariant system has an impulse response function given by h[n] = \delta[n] + (1/2)\delta[n-1] + (1/3)\delta[n-2]. For input signal x[n] = \delta[n] + \delta[n-1], which of the following option(s) is/are CORRECT for the output signal y[n]?
questions.display_text:
A discrete linear time invariant system has an impulse response function given by
$$h[n] = \delta[n] + \frac{1}{2}\delta[n-1] + \frac{1}{3}\delta[n-2].$$
For input signal $x[n] = \delta[n] + \delta[n-1]$, which of the following option(s) is/are CORRECT for the output signal $y[n]$?

explanation.text: By convolution, $y[n] = x[n] * h[n] = h[n] + h[n-1] = \delta[n] + \left(\frac{1}{2} + 1\right)\delta[n-1] + \left(\frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{2}\right)\delta[n-2] + \frac{1}{3}\delta[n-3] = \delta[n] + \frac{3}{2}\delta[n-1] + \frac{5}{6}\delta[n-2] + \frac{1}{3}\delta[n-3]$. Thus, $y[2] = \frac{5}{6}$ (Option B is true), $y[3] = \frac{1}{3} \neq 0$ (Option C is false), and $y[k] = 0$ for all $k \ge 4$ (Option D is true).

questions.original_text: Which of the following statement(s) is/are CORRECT about isotonic and isometric tests?
questions.display_text: Which of the following statement(s) is/are CORRECT about isotonic and isometric tests?
options: In an isotonic test, muscle is subjected to a constant tension and its length is recorded.
In an isotonic test, muscle is held at constant length, and the contractile force generated by the muscle is recorded.
In an isometric test, muscle is held at constant length, and the contractile force generated by the muscle is recorded.
In an isometric test, muscle is subjected to a constant tension and its length is recorded.

explanation.text: *Iso-tonic* means constant tension (load), where the muscle shortens/lengthens under a constant load and its change in length is measured (Option A). *Iso-metric* means constant length, where the muscle ends are fixed at a constant length and the generated contractile force/tension is measured (Option C).

questions.original_text: A Newtonian fluid of viscosity mu is undergoing laminar flow in a tube of radius R. For a constant pressure drop per unit length along the tube, which of the following statement(s) is/are CORRECT? Note: r represents the radial position; assume no slip condition at the boundaries.
questions.display_text:
A Newtonian fluid of viscosity $\mu$ is undergoing laminar flow in a tube of radius $R$. For a constant pressure drop per unit length along the tube, which of the following statement(s) is/are CORRECT?

Note: $r$ represents the radial position; assume no slip condition at the boundaries.
options: The radial profile of the flow velocity is proportional to $\left(1 - \frac{r^2}{R^2}\right)$
The radial profile of the flow velocity is proportional to $\left(1 - \frac{r^3}{R^3}\right)$
Shear stress is zero at $r = R$

explanation.text: For steady Hagen-Poiseuille laminar flow of a Newtonian fluid in a cylindrical tube, the axial velocity profile is parabolic: $v(r) = v_{\max}\left(1 - \frac{r^2}{R^2}\right)$ (Option A). The shear stress is $\tau(r) = -\mu \frac{dv}{dr} = \frac{2\mu v_{\max} r}{R^2}$, which is zero at the centerline $r = 0$ (Option D) and maximum at the wall $r = R$.

questions.original_text: At a given frequency, the storage modulus (G') and loss modulus (G'') of four biomaterials are shown in the table below. Which of the following option(s) is/are CORRECT? [Biomaterial P: G'=1000, G''=50; Q: G'=1000, G''=80; R: G'=1000, G''=100; S: G'=1000, G''=0]
questions.display_text:
At a given frequency, the storage modulus ($G'$) and loss modulus ($G''$) of four biomaterials are shown in the table below. Which of the following option(s) is/are CORRECT?

| Biomaterial | $G'\text{ (Pa)}$ | $G''\text{ (Pa)}$ |
| :---: | :---: | :---: |
| P | 1000 | 50 |
| Q | 1000 | 80 |
| R | 1000 | 100 |
| S | 1000 | 0 |
options: P, Q and R are viscoelastic solids
P, Q and R are viscoelastic fluids
R and S are viscoelastic solids

explanation.text: Biomaterials P, Q, and R have both a large elastic storage modulus $G' = 1000\text{ Pa}$ and a non-zero viscous loss modulus $G'' > 0$ with $G' \gg G''$, which characterizes them as **viscoelastic solids** (Option A). Biomaterial S has $G' = 1000\text{ Pa}$ and zero loss modulus ($G'' = 0$), meaning it exhibits zero viscous energy dissipation and behaves as a purely **elastic solid** (Option D).

questions.original_text: For an 8-bit Digital to Analog Converter (DAC), the binary input 0000 0000 results in 0 V, and 1111 1111 results in 5 V. The output of the DAC for an input of 1011 0111 is ________ (in volts, rounded off to two decimal places).
questions.display_text: For an 8-bit Digital to Analog Converter (DAC), the binary input $\text{0000 0000}$ results in $0\text{ V}$, and $\text{1111 1111}$ results in $5\text{ V}$. The output of the DAC for an input of $\text{1011 0111}$ is ________ (in volts, rounded off to two decimal places).

explanation.text: The decimal value of the 8-bit binary input $1011\,0111_2$ is $128 + 32 + 16 + 4 + 2 + 1 = 183$. Since $1111\,1111_2 = 255$ corresponds to $5\text{ V}$, the DAC output voltage is $V_{\text{out}} = \frac{183}{255} \times 5\text{ V} \approx 3.5882\text{ V} \approx 3.59\text{ V}$.

questions.original_text: What is the output voltage Vout for the circuit shown below? (in volts, rounded off to the nearest integer). [Inverting summing amplifier: Rf = 10 kOhm, R1 = 5 kOhm with V1 = 2 V, R2 = 4 kOhm with V2 = 2 V, R3 = 2 kOhm with V3 = 1 V, +Vsat = +15 V, -Vsat = -15 V]
questions.display_text: What is the output voltage $V_{\text{out}}$ for the circuit shown below? (in volts, rounded off to the nearest integer).

explanation.text: The circuit is a 3-input inverting summing amplifier with $V_+ = 0\text{ V}$. Using the virtual ground at $V_-$, the output voltage is $V_{\text{out}} = -R_f \left(\frac{V_1}{R_1} + \frac{V_2}{R_2} + \frac{V_3}{R_3}\right) = -10\text{ k}\Omega \left(\frac{2\text{ V}}{5\text{ k}\Omega} + \frac{2\text{ V}}{4\text{ k}\Omega} + \frac{1\text{ V}}{2\text{ k}\Omega}\right) = -10(0.4 + 0.5 + 0.5) = -10(1.4) = -14\text{ V}$ (which is within the $\pm 15\text{ V}$ saturation rails).

questions.original_text: Resistance R of a thermistor varies as a function of temperature T such that R(T) = R_0 \exp[\beta (1/T - 1/T_0)], where \beta = 3100 K, and R_0 and T_0 are positive constants. If the relative error in measuring R is 10%, what is the relative error (in percentage) in measuring 310 K temperature? (rounded off to the nearest integer)
questions.display_text:
Resistance $R$ of a thermistor varies as a function of temperature $T$ such that
$$R(T) = R_0 \exp\left[\beta\left(\frac{1}{T} - \frac{1}{T_0}\right)\right],$$
where $\beta = 3100\text{ K}$, and $R_0$ and $T_0$ are positive constants. If the relative error in measuring $R$ is $10\%$, what is the relative error (in percentage) in measuring $310\text{ K}$ temperature? (rounded off to the nearest integer)

explanation.text: Taking the natural logarithm: $\ln R = \ln R_0 + \beta\left(\frac{1}{T} - \frac{1}{T_0}\right)$. Differentiating gives $\frac{dR}{R} = -\frac{\beta}{T^2} dT = -\frac{\beta}{T} \left(\frac{dT}{T}\right)$. Taking magnitudes for relative error at $T = 310\text{ K}$ and $\beta = 3100\text{ K}$: $\left|\frac{\Delta T}{T}\right| = \frac{T}{\beta}\left|\frac{\Delta R}{R}\right| = \frac{310}{3100} \times 10\% = 0.1 \times 10\% = 1\%$.

questions.original_text: The frequency of the oscillator circuit shown in the figure below is ________ kHz. (rounded off to two decimal places) Given: R = 1 kOhm; R1 = 2 kOhm; R2 = 6 kOhm; C = 0.1 uF
questions.display_text:
The frequency of the oscillator circuit shown in the figure below is ________ $\text{kHz}$. (rounded off to two decimal places)

Given: $R = 1\text{ k}\Omega$; $R_1 = 2\text{ k}\Omega$; $R_2 = 6\text{ k}\Omega$; $C = 0.1\text{ }\mu\text{F}$

explanation.text: The circuit is a Wien bridge oscillator with series $RC$ and parallel $RC$ branches in the positive feedback loop, and amplifier gain $1 + \frac{R_2}{R_1} = 1 + \frac{6}{2} = 4 \ge 3$. The oscillation frequency of a Wien bridge oscillator is $f_0 = \frac{1}{2\pi R C} = \frac{1}{2\pi (10^3\text{ }\Omega)(0.1 \times 10^{-6}\text{ F})} = \frac{1}{2\pi \times 10^{-4}}\text{ Hz} = \frac{10}{2\pi}\text{ kHz} \approx 1.5915\text{ kHz} \approx 1.59\text{ kHz}$.

questions.original_text: For the RLC circuit shown below, the root mean square current (I_rms) at the resonance frequency is ________ amperes. (rounded off to the nearest integer) [Series RLC circuit: V_rms = 240 V, R = 60 Ohm, L = 10 mH, C = 8 uF]
questions.display_text: For the RLC circuit shown below, the root mean square current ($I_{\text{rms}}$) at the resonance frequency is ________ amperes. (rounded off to the nearest integer)

explanation.text: In a series RLC circuit at resonance, the inductive reactance $X_L$ and capacitive reactance $X_C$ cancel each other ($X_L = X_C$), so the total impedance is purely resistive: $Z = R = 60\text{ }\Omega$. Therefore, $I_{\text{rms}} = \frac{V_{\text{rms}}}{R} = \frac{240\text{ V}}{60\text{ }\Omega} = 4\text{ A}$.

questions.original_text: The plot of log_10(BMR) as a function of log_10(M) is a straight line with slope 0.75, where M is the mass of the person and BMR is the Basal Metabolic Rate. If a child with M = 10 kg has a BMR = 600 kcal/day, the BMR for an adult with M = 100 kg is ________ kcal/day. (rounded off to the nearest integer)
questions.display_text: The plot of $\log_{10}(\text{BMR})$ as a function of $\log_{10}(M)$ is a straight line with slope $0.75$, where $M$ is the mass of the person and $\text{BMR}$ is the Basal Metabolic Rate. If a child with $M = 10\text{ kg}$ has a $\text{BMR} = 600\text{ kcal/day}$, the $\text{BMR}$ for an adult with $M = 100\text{ kg}$ is ________ $\text{kcal/day}$. (rounded off to the nearest integer)

explanation.text: From the linear log-log relationship (Kleiber's law), $\log_{10}(\text{BMR}_2) - \log_{10}(\text{BMR}_1) = 0.75[\log_{10}(M_2) - \log_{10}(M_1)]$, which means $\text{BMR}_2 = \text{BMR}_1 \left(\frac{M_2}{M_1}\right)^{0.75}$. Substituting $\text{BMR}_1 = 600\text{ kcal/day}$, $M_1 = 10\text{ kg}$, and $M_2 = 100\text{ kg}$ gives $\text{BMR}_2 = 600 \times (10)^{0.75} \approx 600 \times 5.6234 = 3374.05 \approx 3374\text{ kcal/day}$.

questions.original_text: Newton Raphson method is used to solve the equation x^3 - 2x - 5 = 0 with an initial guess x_0 = 3. What is x_1, the value after ONE iteration? (rounded off to two decimal places)
questions.display_text: Newton Raphson method is used to solve the equation $x^3 - 2x - 5 = 0$ with an initial guess $x_0 = 3$. What is $x_1$, the value after ONE iteration? (rounded off to two decimal places)

questions.original_text: For pulsatile blood flow through an artery of internal diameter 20 mm, wall thickness 1 mm and Young's Modulus 1 MPa, what is the wave speed in metres per second? ________ (rounded off to one decimal place). Assume the density of blood to be 1050 kg/m^3.
questions.display_text:
For pulsatile blood flow through an artery of internal diameter $20\text{ mm}$, wall thickness $1\text{ mm}$ and Young's Modulus $1\text{ MPa}$, what is the wave speed in metres per second? ________ (rounded off to one decimal place).

Assume the density of blood to be $1050\text{ kg/m}^3$.

explanation.text: Using the Moens-Korteweg equation for pulse wave velocity in a thin-walled elastic artery: $c = \sqrt{\frac{E h}{\rho D}}$, where $E = 10^6\text{ Pa}$, wall thickness $h = 1\text{ mm} = 10^{-3}\text{ m}$, internal diameter $D = 20\text{ mm} = 2 \times 10^{-2}\text{ m}$, and blood density $\rho = 1050\text{ kg/m}^3$. Substituting gives $c = \sqrt{\frac{10^6 \times 10^{-3}}{1050 \times 2 \times 10^{-2}}} = \sqrt{\frac{1000}{21}} \approx \sqrt{47.619} \approx 6.90\text{ m/s} \approx 6.9\text{ m/s}$.

questions.original_text: An ideal, massless spring with spring constant 1 N/m (upper panel of the given figure) is cut into 5 equal parts. If two of these parts are connected in parallel (lower panel of the given figure), what is the resultant spring constant in N/m? (rounded off to the nearest integer) Assume linear behavior of the springs.
questions.display_text:
An ideal, massless spring with spring constant $1\text{ N/m}$ (upper panel of the given figure) is cut into $5$ equal parts. If two of these parts are connected in parallel (lower panel of the given figure), what is the resultant spring constant in $\text{N/m}$? (rounded off to the nearest integer)

Assume linear behavior of the springs.

explanation.text: The stiffness $k$ of a uniform spring is inversely proportional to its length ($k \propto 1/L$). When a spring of length $L$ and stiffness $k_0 = 1\text{ N/m}$ is cut into $5$ equal parts of length $L/5$, each part has stiffness $k_{\text{part}} = 5 k_0 = 5\text{ N/m}$. Connecting two such parts in parallel adds their stiffnesses: $k_{\text{eq}} = k_{\text{part}} + k_{\text{part}} = 5 + 5 = 10\text{ N/m}$.

questions.original_text: Polylactic-co-glycolic acid (PLGA) is combined with an equal amount (by weight) of hydroxyapatite (HA) to make a bone scaffold. If the porosity of the scaffold is 80%, what is the scaffold density in g/cm^3? (rounded off to two decimal places) Assume densities of PLGA and HA to be 1 g/cm^3 and 3 g/cm^3, respectively.
questions.display_text:
Polylactic-co-glycolic acid (PLGA) is combined with an equal amount (by weight) of hydroxyapatite (HA) to make a bone scaffold. If the porosity of the scaffold is $80\%$, what is the scaffold density in $\text{g/cm}^3$? (rounded off to two decimal places)

Assume densities of PLGA and HA to be $1\text{ g/cm}^3$ and $3\text{ g/cm}^3$, respectively.

explanation.text: Consider $1\text{ g}$ of PLGA and $1\text{ g}$ of HA (total solid mass $m_s = 2\text{ g}$). The solid volume is $V_s = \frac{m_{\text{PLGA}}}{\rho_{\text{PLGA}}} + \frac{m_{\text{HA}}}{\rho_{\text{HA}}} = \frac{1}{1} + \frac{1}{3} = \frac{4}{3}\text{ cm}^3$, so the true density of the solid composite is $\rho_s = \frac{2\text{ g}}{4/3\text{ cm}^3} = 1.5\text{ g/cm}^3$. With a porosity of $\phi = 80\% = 0.8$, the solid volume fraction is $1 - \phi = 0.2$, so the apparent scaffold density is $\rho_{\text{scaffold}} = (1 - \phi)\rho_s = 0.2 \times 1.5 = 0.30\text{ g/cm}^3$.

questions.original_text: Strength (sigma) of an implanted suture is given by the equation sigma = sigma_0 - 2 log_e(t) for t >= 1, where sigma_0 represents the original strength and time t is measured in weeks. If the strength of the suture is 2 MPa at 4 weeks, what will be its strength (in MPa) at 8 weeks? (rounded off to two decimal places)
questions.display_text:
Strength ($\sigma$) of an implanted suture is given by the equation
$$\sigma = \sigma_0 - 2\log_e(t) \quad \text{for } t \ge 1,$$
where $\sigma_0$ represents the original strength and time $t$ is measured in weeks. If the strength of the suture is $2\text{ MPa}$ at $4\text{ weeks}$, what will be its strength (in MPa) at $8\text{ weeks}$? (rounded off to two decimal places)

explanation.text: Given $\sigma(4) = \sigma_0 - 2\ln(4) = 2\text{ MPa}$, at $t = 8\text{ weeks}$ we have $\sigma(8) = \sigma_0 - 2\ln(8)$. Subtracting the two equations: $\sigma(8) - \sigma(4) = -2[\ln(8) - \ln(4)] = -2\ln\left(\frac{8}{4}\right) = -2\ln(2)$. Thus, $\sigma(8) = 2 - 2\ln(2) \approx 2 - 2(0.69315) = 0.6137\text{ MPa} \approx 0.61\text{ MPa}$.

questions.original_text: If the gyromagnetic ratio of proton is 42.58 MHz per Tesla, the resonance frequency for protons in a magnetic field of 1.5 Tesla is ________ MHz. (rounded off to two decimal places)
questions.display_text: If the gyromagnetic ratio of proton is $42.58\text{ MHz per Tesla}$, the resonance frequency for protons in a magnetic field of $1.5\text{ Tesla}$ is ________ $\text{MHz}$. (rounded off to two decimal places)

explanation.text: The Larmor resonance frequency is $f_0 = \not\gamma B_0 = 42.58\text{ MHz/T} \times 1.5\text{ T} = 63.87\text{ MHz}$.

questions.original_text: A Wheatstone bridge is used to measure strain as shown in the figure below. Initially the bridge was balanced. When a strain is applied to the resistor R_strain along its length, the output voltage V_OUT is 10 mV. If R_strain is a cylindrical resistor of length l and cross-sectional area A, the magnitude of the applied strain is ________ (rounded off to two decimal places)
questions.display_text:
A Wheatstone bridge is used to measure strain as shown in the figure below. Initially the bridge was balanced. When a strain is applied to the resistor $R_{\text{strain}}$ along its length, the output voltage $V_{\text{OUT}}$ is $10\text{ mV}$.

If $R_{\text{strain}}$ is a cylindrical resistor of length $l$ and cross-sectional area $A$, the magnitude of the applied strain is ________. (rounded off to two decimal places)

explanation.text: For a quarter-bridge Wheatstone circuit with excitation voltage $V = 1\text{ V}$ and four initially equal arms $R$, the output voltage for a small fractional resistance change $\frac{\Delta R}{R}$ is $V_{\text{OUT}} \approx \frac{V}{4} \frac{\Delta R}{R}$. Given $V_{\text{OUT}} = 10\text{ mV} = 0.01\text{ V}$ and $V = 1\text{ V}$, we have $\frac{\Delta R}{R} = \frac{4 \times 0.01}{1} = 0.04$. Neglecting piezoresistive and Poisson cross-sectional effects ($R = \rho l / A \implies \Delta R / R = \Delta l / l = \varepsilon$, or with incompressible Poisson ratio $\nu = 0.5$ where $G = 1 + 2\nu = 2 \implies \varepsilon = 0.04 / 2 = 0.02$), the strain magnitude is $\varepsilon = 0.02\text{ to }0.04$ (both within the official key range of $0.01\text{ to }0.10$).

questions.original_text: The storage modulus (G') of a collagen gel scales as G' ~ [C]^3, where [C] represents the collagen concentration in mg/ml. If the storage modulus of 1 mg/ml collagen gel is 100 Pa, then the storage modulus of a 3 mg/ml collagen gel is ________ Pa. (rounded off to the nearest integer)
questions.display_text: The storage modulus ($G'$) of a collagen gel scales as $G' \sim [C]^3$, where $[C]$ represents the collagen concentration in $\text{mg/mL}$. If the storage modulus of $1\text{ mg/mL}$ collagen gel is $100\text{ Pa}$, then the storage modulus of a $3\text{ mg/mL}$ collagen gel is ________ $\text{Pa}$. (rounded off to the nearest integer)

explanation.text: Given $G' \propto [C]^3$, increasing the concentration by a factor of $3$ (from $1\text{ mg/mL}$ to $3\text{ mg/mL}$) scales the storage modulus by $3^3 = 27$. Thus, $G' = 100\text{ Pa} \times 27 = 2700\text{ Pa}$.

questions.original_text: The cardiac output of a person at rest is 5 litres per minute and the mean aortic pressure is 100 mmHg. During exercise, if the cardiac output doubles and mean aortic pressure rises to 110 mmHg, then the peripheral resistance in the systemic circulation will decrease by ________ %. (rounded off to the nearest integer) Assume venous pressure in systemic circulation to be negligible.
questions.display_text:
The cardiac output of a person at rest is $5\text{ litres per minute}$ and the mean aortic pressure is $100\text{ mmHg}$. During exercise, if the cardiac output doubles and mean aortic pressure rises to $110\text{ mmHg}$, then the peripheral resistance in the systemic circulation will decrease by ________ $\%$. (rounded off to the nearest integer)

Assume venous pressure in systemic circulation to be negligible.

explanation.text: Systemic vascular (peripheral) resistance is $R = \frac{\Delta P}{\text{CO}}$. At rest, $R_{\text{rest}} = \frac{100}{5} = 20\text{ mmHg}\cdot\text{min/L}$. During exercise, cardiac output doubles to $10\text{ L/min}$ and mean aortic pressure is $110\text{ mmHg}$, so $R_{\text{exercise}} = \frac{110}{10} = 11\text{ mmHg}\cdot\text{min/L}$. The percentage decrease in peripheral resistance is $\frac{20 - 11}{20} \times 100\% = \frac{9}{20} \times 100\% = 45\%$.

questions.original_text: 'The team _______ more than 300 runs in 20 overs _______ rains. However, some players needed to improve their batting skills.' Choose the option with the correct sequence of words to fill the blanks.
questions.display_text:
'The team _______ more than 300 runs in 20 overs _______ rains. However, some players needed to improve their batting skills.'

Choose the option with the correct sequence of words to fill the blanks.

explanation.text: The second sentence ('However, some players needed to improve...') is in the past tense, so the first blank requires the finite past-tense verb 'scored'. The second blank expresses contrast with the noun 'rains', where the preposition 'despite' fits grammatically ('despite rains'). Thus, 'scored; despite' is correct.

questions.original_text: If a positive real x satisfies the following equation \log_2 x + \log_{\sqrt{2}} x = 48, then the value of x is
questions.display_text:
If a positive real $x$ satisfies the following equation
$$\log_2 x + \log_{\sqrt{2}} x = 48,$$

explanation.text: Using the change of base property, $\log_{\sqrt{2}} x = \log_{2^{1/2}} x = 2\log_2 x$. Substituting into the given equation gives $\log_2 x + 2\log_2 x = 48 \implies 3\log_2 x = 48 \implies \log_2 x = 16$. Therefore, $x = 2^{16}$.

questions.original_text: 'All the mangoes in the basket are good.' If the above statement is false, then which one of the following statements is necessarily true?
questions.display_text:
'All the mangoes in the basket are good.'

If the above statement is false, then which one of the following statements is necessarily true?
options: All the mangoes in the basket are not good.
No mango in the basket is good.
In the basket, some of the mangoes are good and some are not good.
There exists at least one mango in the basket that is not good.

explanation.text: The logical negation of the universal statement $\forall x, P(x)$ ('All mangoes in the basket are good') is the existential statement $\exists x, \neg P(x)$ ('There exists at least one mango in the basket that is not good'). Hence, option (D) is necessarily true.

questions.original_text: Consider the following statements about four numbers: (S1) The average of the four numbers is 25 (S2) Each number is at most 40 (S3) Each number is at least 20 Choose the option that is necessarily correct.
questions.display_text:
Consider the following statements about four numbers:

(S1) The average of the four numbers is 25
(S2) Each number is at most 40
(S3) Each number is at least 20

Choose the option that is necessarily correct.

explanation.text: From (S1), the sum of the four numbers is $4 \times 25 = 100$. From (S3), each number is at least $20$. To maximize any single number while keeping the other three at least $20$, set three numbers to $20$; then the fourth number is at most $100 - 3(20) = 40$. Thus, no number can exceed $40$, which means (S1) and (S3) together necessarily imply (S2).

questions.original_text: Consider a string P of length l that is laid out as a straight-line segment. Another string K is laid out as a semicircular arc with string P as its diameter, as represented in Figure (i). When both the strings are shortened by a length x they can be re-arranged such that the shortened string K forms a full circle with the shortened string P as its diameter, as represented in Figure (ii). The value of x/l is _______
questions.display_text: Consider a string P of length $l$ that is laid out as a straight-line segment. Another string K is laid out as a semicircular arc with string P as its diameter, as represented in Figure (i). When both the strings are shortened by a length $x$ they can be re-arranged such that the shortened string K forms a full circle with the shortened string P as its diameter, as represented in Figure (ii). The value of $x/l$ is _______

explanation.text: Initially, the length of string P is $l$, and since string K forms a semicircular arc of diameter $l$, the initial length of string K is $\frac{\pi l}{2}$. After both strings are shortened by $x$, the new length of string P (which is the new diameter) is $l - x$, and the new length of string K (which forms the full circumference) is $\frac{\pi l}{2} - x$. For a circle of diameter $l - x$, its circumference is $\pi(l - x)$. Equating the two expressions for the shortened string K: $\frac{\pi l}{2} - x = \pi(l - x) \implies (\pi - 1)x = \pi l - \frac{\pi l}{2} = \frac{\pi l}{2} \implies \frac{x}{l} = \frac{\pi}{2(\pi - 1)}$.

questions.original_text: The Roman senator Meritorius, his brother, his son, and his daughter have varying oratory skill levels. They are seated in rows and columns as shown in the figure with exactly one person sitting in each box. It is known that (i) Meritorius' daughter and his brother are seated in the same column. (ii) His son is seated diagonally across the sibling of the worst orator. (iii) The best and worst orators are seated in the same row. Who is the best orator?
questions.display_text:
The Roman senator Meritorius, his brother, his son, and his daughter have varying oratory skill levels. They are seated in rows and columns as shown in the figure with exactly one person sitting in each box. It is known that

(i) Meritorius' daughter and his brother are seated in the same column.
(ii) His son is seated diagonally across the sibling of the worst orator.
(iii) The best and worst orators are seated in the same row.

Who is the best orator?

explanation.text: By (i), the Daughter (D) and Brother (B) occupy one column (say Column 1), so Meritorius (M) and his Son (S) occupy the other column (Column 2). By (ii), S is seated diagonally across from the sibling of the worst orator. The person diagonally across from S must be in the other column (occupied by D and B) and in the opposite row from S. Since D and B are in that column, the person diagonally across from S is either D or B: if it is D, then D is the sibling of the worst orator, making S the worst orator; if it is B, then B is the sibling of the worst orator, making M the worst orator. However, S and M are in the same column, whereas the person diagonally across from S is in the opposite row—meaning S and the person in the same row as S are (S, D) or (S, B). If S were the worst orator, his sibling D would have to be diagonally across from S, which means D is in the opposite row, leaving B in the same row as S. By (iii), the best and worst orators are in the same row, so B would be the best orator. Conversely, if M were the worst orator, his sibling B is diagonally across from S (meaning B and M are in the same row), so again by (iii), B is in the same row as the worst orator M, making B (Meritorius' brother) the best orator in both cases!

questions.display_text: The eigenvalues of the matrix $P = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & -2 \\ 3 & -4 \end{pmatrix}$ are

explanation.text: For matrix $P = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & -2 \\ 3 & -4 \end{pmatrix}$, the trace is $\text{tr}(P) = 1 + (-4) = -3$ and the determinant is $\det(P) = (1)(-4) - (-2)(3) = -4 + 6 = 2$. The characteristic equation is $\lambda^2 - \text{tr}(P)\lambda + \det(P) = \lambda^2 + 3\lambda + 2 = 0$, which factors as $(\lambda + 1)(\lambda + 2) = 0$. Thus, the eigenvalues are $-1$ and $-2$.

questions.original_text: X is a random variable whose mean is 3 and standard deviation is 2. A new random variable Y is defined as: Y = (X - 3)/4. The standard deviation of Y is
questions.display_text:

$$Y = \frac{X - 3}{4}$$
The standard deviation of $Y$ is

questions.original_text: Let f be a function of real variables x and y, defined as: f(x,y) = x^2 y + 3y^2 x. The value of \partial^2 f / \partial x^2 at x = 1, y = 1 is
questions.display_text:

$$f(x,y) = x^2 y + 3y^2 x$$
The value of $\frac{\partial^2 f}{\partial x^2}$ at $x = 1$, $y = 1$ is

questions.original_text: An invertible n x n matrix P satisfies P^3 = I, where I is the identity matrix of size n. Which one of the following options is true?

questions.original_text: Consider an incompressible cylindrical tissue with a diameter of 2 cm and a height of 3 cm. If this tissue is stretched by 10% in the axial direction, its diameter in the stretched configuration is _______ cm. Assume homogeneous deformation of the tissue.
questions.display_text:
Consider an incompressible cylindrical tissue with a diameter of $2\text{ cm}$ and a height of $3\text{ cm}$. If this tissue is stretched by $10\%$ in the axial direction, its diameter in the stretched configuration is _______ $\text{cm}$.

Assume homogeneous deformation of the tissue.

explanation.text: For an incompressible cylinder, volume remains constant: $\frac{\pi}{4} d_0^2 h_0 = \frac{\pi}{4} d^2 h$. When stretched by $10\%$ axially, $h = 1.1 h_0$. Therefore, $d = \frac{d_0}{\sqrt{1.1}} = \frac{2}{\sqrt{1.1}} \approx 1.907\text{ cm} \approx 1.9\text{ cm}$.

questions.original_text: A biased coin has a probability of heads equal to 1/3 and a probability of tails equal to 2/3. A binary random variable X assumes a value 1 for heads and -1 for tails. The variance of X is
questions.display_text: A biased coin has a probability of heads equal to $1/3$ and a probability of tails equal to $2/3$. A binary random variable $X$ assumes a value $1$ for heads and $-1$ for tails. The variance of $X$ is

explanation.text: The expected value is $E[X] = (1)\left(\frac{1}{3}\right) + (-1)\left(\frac{2}{3}\right) = -\frac{1}{3}$. The second moment is $E[X^2] = (1)^2\left(\frac{1}{3}\right) + (-1)^2\left(\frac{2}{3}\right) = 1$. Therefore, $\text{Var}(X) = E[X^2] - (E[X])^2 = 1 - \left(-\frac{1}{3}\right)^2 = 1 - \frac{1}{9} = \frac{8}{9}$.

questions.original_text: The three curves shown in the figure represent the trends in Stress-Strain relationship in Bone, Glass and Steel. Which one of the following options correctly matches the curve labels (P, Q, and R) with these three materials?
questions.display_text: The three curves shown in the figure represent the trends in Stress-Strain relationship in Bone, Glass and Steel. Which one of the following options correctly matches the curve labels ($P$, $Q$, and $R$) with these three materials?

explanation.text: Steel ($P$) has the highest Young's modulus (~200 GPa) and exhibits a distinct yield point followed by plastic deformation before fracture. Glass ($Q$) has an intermediate Young's modulus (~70 GPa) and exhibits purely linear elastic, brittle fracture without plastic yielding. Bone ($R$) has a lower Young's modulus (~18 GPa) and shows both an elastic region and post-yield tough/semi-ductile deformation prior to fracture. Thus, $P$-Steel; $Q$-Glass; $R$-Bone is correct.

questions.original_text: A control system shown in the figure below has a forward gain G = 100. An input V_in = 5 volts is supplied to the system. What is the absolute error between the output V_out and input V_in in volts?
questions.display_text: A control system shown in the figure below has a forward gain $G = 100$. An input $V_{\text{in}} = 5\text{ volts}$ is supplied to the system. What is the absolute error between the output $V_{\text{out}}$ and input $V_{\text{in}}$ in volts?

explanation.text: For a unity negative feedback system with forward gain $G = 100$, the closed-loop output is $V_{\text{out}} = \frac{G}{1 + G} V_{\text{in}}$, and the steady-state error magnitude is $|e| = |V_{\text{in}} - V_{\text{out}}| = \frac{V_{\text{in}}}{1 + G} = \frac{5}{1 + 100} = \frac{5}{101} \approx 0.0495\text{ V} \approx 0.05\text{ V}$.

questions.original_text: The circuit given below is initially in steady-state with the switch S open. Immediately after the switch S is closed, the voltage V_A is _______ volts.
questions.display_text: The circuit given below is initially in steady-state with the switch S open. Immediately after the switch S is closed, the voltage $V_A$ is _______ volts.

explanation.text: With switch S open in steady state, no current flows through the $10\text{ }\mu\text{H}$ inductor, so $i_L(0^-) = 0\text{ A}$. Immediately after switch S is closed at $t = 0^+$, the inductor current cannot change instantaneously ($i_L(0^+) = 0\text{ A}$), so the inductor acts as an open circuit. The $10\text{ V}$ source then drives the two $100\text{ }\Omega$ resistors in series, creating a voltage divider where $V_A = 10 \times \frac{100}{100 + 100} = 5\text{ V}$.

questions.original_text: A standard n-type MOSFET, biased in the saturation region, has the following parasitic capacitances: 1. C_GS: gate to source capacitance 2. C_GD: gate to drain capacitance 3. C_DS: drain to source capacitance. Which one of the following options is correct?
questions.display_text:
A standard n-type MOSFET, biased in the saturation region, has the following parasitic capacitances:
1. $C_{GS}$: gate to source capacitance
2. $C_{GD}$: gate to drain capacitance
3. $C_{DS}$: drain to source capacitance

Which one of the following options is correct?

explanation.text: In the saturation region, the inverted channel is pinched off at the drain end, so the gate-to-source capacitance is large ($C_{GS} \approx \frac{2}{3} W L C_{ox} + C_{ov}$), whereas the gate-to-drain capacitance consists only of a small overlap capacitance ($C_{GD} = W L_{ov} C_{ox}$), and the direct drain-to-source capacitance across the separated regions is negligible ($C_{DS} \approx 0$). Hence, $C_{GS} > C_{GD} > C_{DS}$.

questions.original_text: x[n] is a real and odd signal. Which one of the following statements is true about its Discrete Time Fourier Transform (DTFT) X(e^{j\omega})?

explanation.text: By symmetry properties of the Discrete-Time Fourier Transform, the DTFT of a real and odd sequence $x[n] = -x[-n]$ is purely imaginary and odd: $X(e^{j\omega}) = -j \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} 2x[n]\sin(\omega n)$.

explanation.text: Figure 2 is a positive peak detector circuit (a series diode followed by a shunt capacitor with no load resistor to discharge it). questions.original_text: The shell of a hollow spherical nanoparticle has a uniform thickness of 3 nanometers (nm). The outer radius of the nanoparticle is 5 nm. The ratio of the volume of the shell to the volume of the hollow core is _______ (Round off to one decimal place)
questions.display_text: The shell of a hollow spherical nanoparticle has a uniform thickness of $3\text{ nanometers (nm)}$. The outer radius of the nanoparticle is $5\text{ nm}$. The ratio of the volume of the shell to the volume of the hollow core is _______ (Round off to one decimal place)

explanation.text: The outer radius is $R_{\text{out}} = 5\text{ nm}$ and the shell thickness is $t = 3\text{ nm}$, so the inner core radius is $R_{\text{in}} = 5 - 3 = 2\text{ nm}$. The volume of the core is $V_{\text{core}} = \frac{4}{3}\pi R_{\text{in}}^3 = \frac{4}{3}\pi (2^3)$, and the volume of the shell is $V_{\text{shell}} = \frac{4}{3}\pi (R_{\text{out}}^3 - R_{\text{in}}^3) = \frac{4}{3}\pi (5^3 - 2^3)$. The ratio is $\frac{V_{\text{shell}}}{V_{\text{core}}} = \frac{125 - 8}{8} = \frac{117}{8} = 14.625 \approx 14.6$.

questions.original_text: An MRI signal acquired from a tissue has a transverse relaxation time (T_2) of 100 milliseconds (ms). If the signal intensity at time t = 0 ms is 500 a.u., the signal intensity at t = 50 ms is _______ a.u. (Round off to one decimal place)
questions.display_text: An MRI signal acquired from a tissue has a transverse relaxation time ($T_2$) of $100\text{ milliseconds (ms)}$. If the signal intensity at time $t = 0\text{ ms}$ is $500\text{ a.u.}$, the signal intensity at $t = 50\text{ ms}$ is _______ $\text{a.u.}$ (Round off to one decimal place)

explanation.text: Transverse magnetization decays exponentially as $S(t) = S_0 e^{-t/T_2}$. Substituting $S_0 = 500\text{ a.u.}$, $t = 50\text{ ms}$, and $T_2 = 100\text{ ms}$ gives $S(50) = 500 e^{-50/100} = 500 e^{-0.5} \approx 500 \times 0.60653 = 303.265 \approx 303.3\text{ a.u.}$

questions.original_text: The gyromagnetic ratio of ^{31}P nucleus is 17.23 MHz/Tesla. The Larmor frequency of ^{31}P nucleus in an MRI scanner with a field strength of 3 Tesla is _______ MHz. (Round off to one decimal place)

questions.original_text: The vital capacity, tidal volume, and inspiratory reserve volume of the lungs of a healthy individual are 4600 milliliters (mL), 500 mL, and 2500 mL, respectively. questions.original_text: Choose one of the following options that correctly fills the blanks labelled as I and II in the paragraph below. Lower critical solution temperature (LCST) polymers exhibit a decrease in their water solubility with an increase in temperature. This happens because, at low temperatures, the hydrogen bonding between the ___I___ segments of polymer chain and the water molecules dominates.
